record_notes.DCP-LETT-13807: Monday evening in April 1850–January 1851, crossing period boundary. Six blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Four separately enumerated specimen taxa safely arrived, one prior arcuatum valve distinguished. Woodward most likely recipient from British Museum provenance; editorial summary JWF conflicts with title/apparatus, not a certain Flower identity. Current laevis or unguis uncertainty retained despite later taxonomic distinction. Date and recipient confidence held; no exact receipt day or incoming cover text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1392: March 3, supplied 1851, inferred Woodward recipient through Aptychus discussion. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Darwin says monograph finished and printed, returns mostly named specimens with loose-valve warning. Aptychus arrived already broken, no other specimens injured; do not attribute breakage to Darwin. Return in progress not museum receipt. Printed status is author claim distinct from later distribution. Missing incoming request not required to explain unsolicited return notice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1435: June 9, supplied 1851. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Woodward showed paper and Darwin recalls reading/making now-lost extract, but exact paper and Annales venue uncertain; asks reference, attachment, travel and nutrition of supposed male Argonaut. Later 1852 correction identifies an arm, not whole male; no retrospective correction of current belief. Paper read at society in1845 and printed1851, probable earlier separate issue not guaranteed exact access. Summary journal volume22/pages9–22 conflicts with bibliography volume20/pages9–21, retained as source discrepancy.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1570: May6,1854 from later1910 catalogue. One cataloguer-authored block, four footnotes and bibliography; original letter not found.1909 exhibition guide reports Darwin refusal of Hippuritidae bridge, but no verbatim Darwin body. Carpenter1844 in guide versus1843 article in apparatus retained. This is an unavailable letter represented by synopsis, not a one-paragraph Darwin transcription or target voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1477: March14,1852, single long Sydney Mail transcription block with seven footnotes and bibliography. Covington June1851 letter received a couple of months earlier, approximate not fixed January14; Berrill note two days ago means March12. Darwin forwarded Syms letter to brother, text missing here and historical permission judgment not an agent instruction. Gold-trade trip and comparative behavior questions unanswered, not proof of journey or moral superiority. Barnacle book published and recent specimen examination established; second volume future. Later deBeer rendering differs, possible normalization not authority to alter preserved text. Sulivan visit recalled; apparatus November27,1851 event distinct from current date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1538: October21,1853 single long Sydney Mail block, thirteen footnotes and bibliography. Explicit Covington May25,1853 letter received October11 at Down, voyage itinerary traced from now-missing letter. Nugget wish not discovery. Mundy book read lately, apparatus dates three volumes May17–July2; broad reading claim not evidence every Australian book read. Barnacle second volume unfinished. FitzRoy widowhood and money loss reported, Mellersh fighting reported, war feared rather than later1854 intervention known. Pambala and He for Fuegia flagged transcription errors by editors; preserve exact source plus correction layer, do not silently substitute. Indigenous person identified in apparatus, not masculine historical identity inferred from typo.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1637: February28,1855. Two blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Covington August8,1854 letter arrived about six weeks earlier, no exact January day. Family comparison, rent and loyalty received as correspondent report; embedded loyal-subjects quotation is Covington voice, not original Darwin formulation. Mackenzie seen/heard, published book mentioned but no explicit own reading. London stay and frost observed; FitzRoy department and remarriage reported, new wife not seen. Sulivan visit before departure still future, children count uncertain six or seven. War criticism and national pride historical author opinions. Source degree notation 0o retained; no modern precision inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13787: Copy dated26 in one of91 mutually exclusive monthly dates, December1843–April1846 OR September1855–October1860, questioned header. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Missing Hooker letter arrived this morning after two or three missing Darwin letters; refuses offered unidentified plant. No exact year, month, plant or full incoming body. Address apparatus also mentions second half1853 usage, not included in encoded alternatives; retain inconsistency without adding an invented exact date. Salutation limits are inference, not hard event timestamp. Some alternatives after Origin; date/period hold. Hooker rejection report is not a direct incoming Cresy prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1677: April29, supplied1853, copy. Six blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Missing Cresy note and section received and used; siphon, joint and brick ribs proposed, not built. Raw MathML twice gives1 plus one-half inches, distinct from three-inch pump, nine-inch ribs and9d/foot cost. Lastell in copy, Laslet marginal change, Laslett identified in apparatus kept as layers. Missing Cresy drawing not recreated from verbal interpretation; silence would indicate assent only by Darwin proposed convention. Parallel Gardeners Chronicle question sent, not same incoming source. Later summer absence not already completed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1682: May15, supplied1853 ALS. Two blocks and footnote. Burgess and Key visit now completed: flat coated hose unsuitable for suction, gutta percha unsuitable frequent motion; leather nearly20pounds rejected. Siphon abandoned, ordinary tank with pump intended, not completed installation. Later June/August gutta-percha pipe payments refer apparatus and do not undo rejection of movable hose. Earlier April and July builder accounts are separate dated evidence, not proof every planned detail constructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1427: May6, supplied1851 copy. Two blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Thanks missing discovery report, initially accepts probable palaeozoic footprints but has not seen specimens and cannot come to town. Owen referral and Jukes expertise recommendations, not completed expert examination. Return collection hopes conditional. Later concretions correction not known here; copy Disnurr spelling differs recipient identity.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1428: May15, supplied1851 copy. Three blocks, two footnotes, bibliography and raw HTML. Two missing notes and box now received; revises supposed footprints to concretionary forms after seeing analogous structures. Encourages collecting but advises retaining comparisons before sending. Spare Admiralty Manual offered if wanted, not yet sent or received. Raw12 in porterage sentence has no fractional markup; intended half remains rendering hold. Stamps accounting not silently normalized.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1436: June13, supplied1851 copy. Five blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography. Offers Forbes introduction/dredging advice but does not know supplier or show visit occurred. Fossil bones sought regardless kangaroo identity; no later receipt proved, apparatus finds none. Animal preservation instructions and two cirripede requests prospective; rude tracing enclosure absent. Dash/question-mark copyist unreadable word not reconstructed. Ibla and possible Scalpellum identifications editorial confidence differs. Thanks offer of gift, not actual gift custody.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1188: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Wednesday July5 OR July12,1848, two distinct alternatives inferred before Buckland reply July15. Darwin has written a recommendation to Buckland despite described mutual prejudice; thinks it can do no harm, does not know actual result yet. Cresy had requested help; source request and actual recommendation text missing. Advises Cresy call but no completed interview here. Personal characterization of Buckland attributed Darwin opinion. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1191: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Saturday night assigned July15,1848 only by assuming immediate writing when Buckland July15 note received. Incoming composition date is not arrival date; same-night assignment not independently proved. Cresy own note arrived this morning, a distinct input whose text is missing. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1192: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Thursday assigned July20,1848 from planned Saturday seaside departure and independently recorded July22 Swanage journey. Missing Cresy thanks and decision against further letters acknowledged. Darwin promises to speak to Owen, De la Beche and Hutton when next seen, not completed advocacy. Planned naturalists party cancelled/not invited because health and expected confinement. Seaside departure still prospective in body; later actual trip supports date but does not supply extra contemporary details. No incoming Cresy endpoint.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1238: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Sunday morning assigned June24,1849 from Cresy letter of22nd, final Malvern Sunday and June30 return. Missing June22 letter forwarded from Down, actual arrival not separately dated. Darwin explicitly states March10 arrival at Malvern, firmer than retrospective nearly-two-month estimates elsewhere. King good wishes based on testimonials/writings/secondhand reports; refuses canvassing because not personally acquainted, but conditionally offers to mention him to Owen. Returning documents avoids copies; texts unavailable. Return home beginning next month intended; actual June30 later. Possible Franklin-search canvassing purpose editorial conjecture, not established contents of missing appeal.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1237: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 30, 1849. Explicitly writes from Malvern despite Down dateline; address is not physical location. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1314: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 21, supplied 1850. Missing Woodward Aptychus history/sketches already read, combined with a few seen specimens to judge d Orbigny view unlikely; museum inspection still future. Norwich and Grey Chalk material examined, descriptions/comparisons provisional; later definitive names and possible specimen identities remain editorial. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1370: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 23, 1850. Distinguishes Covington March 12 letter received August 25 from box arriving yesterday November 22; both now known, but original letter absent. At least seven kinds, curious new species identification only probable in later apparatus. Packing newspaper names read, not full news text preserved. Current seven children/four sons and more expected, emigration conditional on feared gold effects, not actual emigration or economic certainty. Colonial praise and railway assertions are historical author claims, not modern validated facts. Future1852manual reading cannot be backdated. Preserve Sydney Mail transcription provenance shared with1237.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
